items.question: Atropine blocks which type of receptor?
items.explanation: Atropine is a competitive muscarinic (M) receptor antagonist, causing tachycardia, mydriasis, dry mouth.

items.question: Pilocarpine is used in glaucoma because it causes?
items.explanation: Pilocarpine (muscarinic agonist) causes miosis and ciliary contraction, improving aqueous humour outflow.

items.question: Mirabegron treats overactive bladder by acting as a?
items.explanation: Mirabegron is a selective beta-3 agonist relaxing the detrusor, an alternative to antimuscarinics.

items.question: Why does phenylephrine cause reflex bradycardia?
options: Alpha-1 vasoconstriction raises BP, triggering baroreceptor vagal reflex
items.explanation: Phenylephrine raises BP via alpha-1 vasoconstriction; baroreceptors trigger reflex vagal bradycardia.

items.question: Which clinical trial phase first establishes safety and pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers?
items.explanation: Phase I trials assess safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics, usually in a small group of healthy volunteers.

Q: Atropine blocks which type of receptor?

Q: Pilocarpine is used in glaucoma because it causes?

Q: Mirabegron treats overactive bladder by acting as a?
Ans: Beta-3 agonist

Q: Why does phenylephrine cause reflex bradycardia?
Ans: Alpha-1 vasoconstriction raises BP, triggering baroreceptor vagal reflex
Why: Phenylephrine raises BP via alpha-1 vasoconstriction; baroreceptors trigger reflex vagal bradycardia.

Q: Which clinical trial phase first establishes safety and pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers?
